newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica's Mpumalanga grants first gambling license.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica's Mpumalanga grants first gambling license.

text.p: South Africa's Mpumalanga province on Wednesday granted the first legal gambling licence in South Africa to the Global Resorts South Africa consortium, which it shortlisted in January.

Legislation passed last year legalises casino gambling in South Africa for the first time. Provinces have been given the reins to award licences to companies keen to grab a slice of the multi-billion-rand industry.

Global Resorts Southern Highveld, a unit of the group, said it planned to build a 200 million rand casino and country club resort in the southern highveld region of Mpumalanga. The complex is expected to be completed in the middle of next year.
A temporary casino at the venue will be completed by September this year.

"We are proud to be granted the historic licence to operate the first legalised casino in Mpumalanga and in South Africa under the new gaming legislation," GRSA chief executive officer Ernie Joubert told reporters.
GRSA, whose investors include Rand Merchant Bank, Genbel South Africa and Malaysia's Mycom Berhad, also has a black empowerment shareholder Rethabile National Investors.

This black grouping, which represents the Mineworkers Investment Company and the Women's Development Businesses' initiative, will control 50 percent of the licence value of every licence granted, GRSA said.

Mpumalanga province said it hoped to issue a further two licences soon. Tsogo Sun, a joint-venture between a black consortium and South African Breweries hotels unit Southern Sun, was selected in January for resorts in the cities of Witbank and Nelspruit.
The fourth licence would be decided upon later.
GRSA said it would be making a bids for gambling licences in the populous Gauteng province which last month opened its bidding process.
